entries.title: From scarcity into famine
entries.literal_meaning: To go from high prices into famine.
entries.explanation: A change meant to escape difficulty leads into something worse. Here କାନ୍ତାର is the dictionary’s famine sense, not its separate forest sense.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗୋଟିଏ ଅସୁବିଧାରୁ ମୁକୁଳିବାକୁ ଯାଇ ଆହୁରି ବଡ଼ ଅସୁବିଧାରେ ପଡ଼ିବା। ଏଠାରେ କାନ୍ତାରର ଅର୍ଥ ଦୁର୍ଭିକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: A shop changes to a cheaper supplier, then loses more because deliveries repeatedly fail. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The food-scarcity image supplies the comparison; no particular famine or historical event is identified.

entries.title: By whatever means
entries.explanation: The expression describes pursuing a result by every available means. Depending on context, it can suggest determination or a willingness to use unfair methods.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେକୌଣସି ଉପାୟରେ କାମ ହାସଲ କରିବା। ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଅନୁସାରେ ଏଥିରେ ଚେଷ୍ଟାର ଦୃଢ଼ତା ବା ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଉପାୟର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ରହିପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: A character in a story resolves to win the contest by persuasion, pressure or a clever plan. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: This is an adverbial idiom in the dictionary, not a complete narrative proverb or an endorsement of deceit.

entries.title: Feeding one at another’s expense
entries.literal_meaning: Like killing grasshoppers to feed a myna.
entries.explanation: The image exposes a benefit obtained by making another bear the loss. The explanation follows the contrast between the creature killed and the one nourished.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜଣକର କ୍ଷତି କରି ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣକର ଲାଭ କରାଇବା। ଝିଣ୍ଟିକା ମରେ, ବଣି ଖାଇ ବଞ୍ଚେ—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଫଳ ହିଁ କଥାଟିର ମୂଳ।
entries.usage_example: A manager improves one team’s figures by shifting its unfinished work onto another team. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the expression ପ୍ରବଚନ. Its linked insect and bird entries support the literal image; the social application is editorial.

entries.title: Even river sand runs out
entries.literal_meaning: If one sits and consumes, even the river’s sand runs out.
entries.explanation: Even a large store can be exhausted if it is continually used without replenishment. The exaggerated sand image makes the scale of the reserve irrelevant.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭଣ୍ଡାର ଯେତେ ବଡ଼ ହେଲେ ବି କେବଳ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରି ଚାଲିଲେ ତାହା ସରିଯାଏ। ଭରଣା ନହେଲେ ନଈର ବାଲି ପରି ପ୍ରଚୁର ଜିନିଷ ବି ଶେଷ ହେବ ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଇଛି।
entries.usage_example: A club repeatedly pays expenses from its reserve but collects no new contributions. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source places this under consuming savings without earning. It should not be used to blame people unable to work or to deny their need for support.

entries.title: Words travel farther than drums
entries.odia: ଚମବାଇଦ କୋଶେ, ତୁଣ୍ଡ ବାଇଦ ଶହସ୍ର କୋଶ
entries.literal_meaning: A hide-drum carries one kos; the mouth’s drum a thousand kos.
entries.explanation: News passed from person to person can spread much farther than a sound heard at its source. The contrast is deliberate exaggeration, not a measured claim about distance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଢୋଲର ଶବ୍ଦ ଯେତେ ଦୂର ଯାଏ, ଲୋକମୁଖରେ ଚାଲୁଥିବା କଥା ତାଠାରୁ ବହୁ ଦୂର ପହଞ୍ଚେ। ହଜାର କୋଶ କଥାଟି ଏଠାରେ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି।
entries.usage_example: A small announcement at a village gathering is being discussed in distant households the next day. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary’s sense1 is a report or rumour carried by word of mouth. The longer witness is retained; the discovery list gives only its latter idea.

entries.title: Measure farther than you step
entries.literal_meaning: Measure a cubit, then move a span.
entries.explanation: Examine more of the situation than the immediate step requires. The proverb recommends deliberation before acting; careful preparation can reduce risk without guaranteeing safety.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଗକୁ ଭଲଭାବେ ବୁଝି ବିଚାରି ଛୋଟ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ ନେବା। ଯେତିକି କାମ କରିବା, ତାଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଦୂରର ଫଳ ଭାବିବା।
entries.usage_example: Before moving a workshop, its owners check access, costs and likely demand, then try a small temporary space. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary itself explains the longer measure and shorter step. These are traditional body-based measures; no fixed modern conversion is needed here.

entries.title: Harm from what was kept close
entries.literal_meaning: The knife tucked at the waist cuts the throat.
entries.explanation: Something or someone trusted and kept close becomes the source of harm. The dictionary puts the saying beside its figurative sense of cheating.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହାକୁ ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଭରସା କରି ପାଖରେ ରଖିଥାଉ, ସେହିଠାରୁ କ୍ଷତି ହେବା। ଏଠାରେ ଛୁରିର ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବିଶ୍ୱାସଭଙ୍ଗକୁ ବୁଝାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A trusted business partner secretly diverts the shop’s receipts. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Violent imagery describes betrayal; it is not an instruction to harm anyone. The source does not establish a particular origin story.

entries.title: Do not delay a good beginning
entries.explanation: Once a worthwhile action is decided, avoid needless delay. This is encouragement to begin, not a reason to abandon judgment or preparation.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭଲ କାମ କରିବାକୁ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ହେଲେ ଅକାରଣ ବିଳମ୍ବ ନକରିବା। ତରବର ହୋଇ ବିଚାର ଛାଡ଼ିବା ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After agreeing to repair the library’s leaking roof, the volunteers arrange the work promptly. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The Odia dictionary explicitly labels this a Sanskrit proverb. It is included as an expression used in Odia, not claimed as uniquely Odia in origin.

entries.title: A pious appearance that deceives
entries.literal_meaning: A cat as a Vaishnava devotee.
entries.explanation: A show of devotion conceals conduct that contradicts it. The target is the mismatch between appearance and action, not believers as a group.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାହାରେ ଧାର୍ମିକ ବେଶ ଦେଖାଇ ଭିତରେ ତାହାର ବିପରୀତ କାମ କରିବା। ଏହା କପଟ ଆଚରଣର ସମାଲୋଚନା, କୌଣସି ଧର୍ମର ସମସ୍ତ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ଦାବି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A fictional official advertises personal virtue while secretly taking unfair benefits. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The exact dictionary spelling ବଇଷମ is preserved. It is given as a figurative synonym under ଭେଖଧାରୀ ବୈଷ୍ଣବ; no animal fable or historical founder is supplied.
